blocking.what: The case analysis is written on the exact negation $-X[i]$ in $\mathbb{Z}$ and on the type of $X$ and $Y$; the second case is stated as "$-X[i] - 2^n$" without saying that the subtraction is the subtraction of $\mathbb{Z}$ and that the result is then read as a signed $n$-bit value.
blocking.why: The guidelines require every operation on a machine type to be indexed ($+_{(	ext{i8})}$, …) and every symbol to be defined; a bare $-$ inside an integer section is the operation on $\mathbb{R}$ (l.110), which is not what the section means, and the reader cannot tell whether the reduction is a wrap-around or an exact integer subtraction.
blocking.fix: Write the second case as $-X[i] -_{(	ext{i}n)} 2^n$ (or state explicitly that the subtraction is the exact subtraction in $\mathbb{Z}$ followed by the reading of the result modulo $2^n$ as a signed value), and add a where-bullet defining $-_{(	ext{i}n)}$ as the subtraction of the $n$-bit signed type.
